title: Amount of a Late Payment Charge on an Electric Service Agreement Bill
content:
Billing Operations figures the late payment charge on an Electric Service Agreement bill from two quantities: the unpaid portion of the bill and the schedule's late payment charge rate.

## Method

1. **Unpaid portion.** The unpaid portion of the bill is the smaller of the bill's amount and the agreement's outstanding balance (the sum of its bills and charges less the sum of its payments and credits), never below zero, because payments and credits settle the oldest items first and the most recent bill is settled last. The bill concerned is the agreement's most recent bill, the one with the latest bill date; the outstanding balance takes every bill, every charge, every payment and every credit recorded on the agreement.
2. **Charge.** The late payment charge is the schedule's late payment charge rate times the unpaid portion, rounded to the cent, and never less than the schedule's late payment charge minimum when any part of the bill is unpaid.
3. **No charge.** No late payment charge arises when the unpaid portion is zero.
4. **Final figure.** The charge is stated in USD rounded to the cent.

The rate and the minimum are the figures of the schedule the agreement is billed under.

## Worked figures (hypothetical inputs)

Assume a hypothetical schedule with a late payment charge rate of 1.5% and a minimum of 1.00 USD.

| Case | Most recent bill | Outstanding balance | Unpaid portion | Rate times unpaid portion | Charge |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| A | 182.40 | 260.15 | 182.40 (the bill is smaller) | 2.736, rounded 2.74 | 2.74 |
| B | 182.40 | 95.10 | 95.10 (the balance is smaller) | 1.4265, rounded 1.43 | 1.43 |
| C | 182.40 | 40.00 | 40.00 | 0.60 | 1.00 (the minimum) |
| D | 182.40 | minus 12.00 (a credit) | 0.00 | none | no charge |

In case A the balance includes older items, but the unpaid portion cannot exceed the bill itself. In case D the balance is a credit, the unpaid portion is held at zero and no charge arises, so the minimum does not come into play.
